title: The Determinant of a Square Matrix

questions.prompt: What is the determinant of the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$?
The determinant of $\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$ is $ad$ minus ___.
hints: The product of the other diagonal.

questions.prompt: If the determinant of a matrix is zero, the matrix is called ___.
What is the minor $M_{12}$ of the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$?
hints: Delete first row and second column.

The determinant of the remaining $2 \times 2$ matrix is $3 \cdot 0 - 2 \cdot 1 = -2$, wait that's $-2$. But we need to check. After deleting row1 col2, matrix is $\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, determinant $= 3\cdot0 - 2\cdot1 = -2$. But the options say -2 is A. But earlier we computed cofactor for that position was 2 after sign change. The minor itself is -2, not 2. So answer A. Correct.

questions.prompt: In the sign pattern for cofactors, what is the sign of $C_{21}$? (+ or -)
The determinant of a $3 \times 3$ matrix is computed by:
options: B. Expanding by cofactors along a row or column
C. Adding the entries of the main diagonal
D. Finding the inverse and taking its reciprocal
hints: Sum of entries times their cofactors.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The determinant is computed by expanding by cofactors along a row or column.

questions.prompt: To minimize work when computing a determinant, expand along the row or column with the most ___.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Choose the row or column with the most zeros.

questions.prompt: What is the determinant of $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$? (Enter a number)
hints: Expand along first row: $1\cdot C_{11} + 3\cdot C_{12} + (-2)\cdot C_{13}$.

questions.prompt: When expanding a $4 \times 4$ determinant along a column with a single nonzero entry $a_{ij}$, how many $3 \times 3$ determinants must you compute?
hints: Only the cofactor of that nonzero entry is needed.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: You only need to compute the cofactor of that single nonzero entry, which is one $3 \times 3$ determinant.

questions.prompt: The cofactor $C_{13}$ of a $4 \times 4$ matrix has sign ___ (since $1+3=4$, even).
In the $4 \times 4$ example, what was the value of the determinant? (Enter a number)
hints: We expanded along column 3; only $a_{13}=3$ contributed.

questions.prompt: Which operation changes the sign of the determinant?
options: A. Multiplying a row by a scalar
C. Adding a multiple of one row to another
D. Multiplying the entire matrix by a scalar
hints: The determinant becomes negative of the original.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Interchanging two rows changes the sign of the determinant.

questions.prompt: The determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of the entries on the ___ diagonal.
If a $3 \times 3$ matrix has a row of zeros, what is its determinant? (Enter a number)
hints: Expanding along that row yields all zero terms.
Any matrix with a row or column of zeros has determinant zero.
